abstract: Sensory neurons establish intimate connections with the surrounding epidermis, where specialized extracellular matrix (ECM) help maintain neuron-epidermal interactions. However, whether and how this specialized ECM regulates the spatial organization of cortical proteins at these interfaces remains poorly understood. Here, we show a specialized ECM patterns the cortical microtubule regulator EFA-6 at neuron-epidermal interfaces in Caenorhabditis elegans. We show that EFA-6 in the epidermal cortex is enriched adjacent to the neurites of touch receptor neurons, characterized by discrete foci at the distal neurite and a diffuse distribution in the proximal neurite. We identify the specialized ECM components MEC-1 and HIM-4/hemicentin as regulators of EFA-6 spatial patterning at the interface between epidermis and neuronal processes. EFA-6 proteins contain an intrinsically disordered region (IDR) that is necessary and sufficient for EFA-6 targeting to and patterning at the neuron-epidermal interface. Within the IDR, we further identify an 8 residue motif that regulates enrichment and patterning of EFA-6 IDR at this interface. Finally, we find that EFA-6 contributes to age-dependent neurite defects in him-4 mutants. Together, our findings reveal how a specialized extracellular matrix and an intrinsically disordered region coordinate the spatial organization of a cortical MT regulator at neuron-epidermal interface.
